answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a bond in a public ledger before voting on payouts. Voting weight follows bonded value, so splitting one stake across a hundred names adds no influence. A verifier checks each bond is unspent, while a cipher-based commitment protects private details. After a challenge period, the bond flows like a river to its owner; proven fraud makes it forfeit. To flood the system, an attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it, not merely forge names.
